findings.actor: Unauthenticated remote attacker via crafted link or direct request
findings.claim: The `name` query parameter is taken directly from the URL and interpolated unescaped into an HTML response, allowing reflected JavaScript execution in the victim's browser.

evidence.note: greetName returns attacker-controlled URL query value `name` with no validation or escaping, defaulting only when missing
renderGreeting interpolates `name` directly into HTML h1 element via template string with no escaping call
handleGreet renders that value and returns it as text/html, completing reflected-XSS source-to-sink
escapeHtml helper exists but is never called in this cluster, confirming missing output encoding

findings.resource: GET /greet HTML greeting response and `name` query parameter
findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting in greeting via unescaped name parameter
findings.validation: Statically traced flow: URL searchParams.get(name) in greetName to string interpolation in renderGreeting to text/html response in handleGreet with no sanitization or escapeHtml use in between.
